title: Florida AI Laws

reading.body:
Florida's only AI-related law is a resolution recognizing CyberBay as a cybersecurity and AI innovation region, not a rule that governs anyone.

The law, S1816, passed on 2026-03-12. It names a region in the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges the state's cybersecurity preparedness, and affirms public-private collaboration. It creates no obligation, no standard, and no enforcement. A reader looking for Florida's rules on how AI systems are built, deployed, or audited will not find them here.

That distinction matters for AI infrastructure. Data centers and the power they draw are governed by siting, utility, and tax rules, and none of those appear in this data. A single recognition resolution says nothing about whether Florida will ease or restrict the grid connections that AI buildout depends on.

The data covers one law and its enrolled text. It does not show bills that failed, executive orders, agency rules, or local ordinances, so it cannot support a claim that Florida has been inactive or active on AI beyond this one measure.

Florida has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Florida

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1816: CyberBay passed 2026-03-12

    The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Florida. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
